results.title: Nebius Said to Raise Prices for its On-demand Compute Resources Starting October | MemoryMarket - memory prices, market analysis, industry news, research report
highlights:
According to media reports, as Nebius continues to expand its AI infrastructure globally, the company will raise prices for some of its on-demand computing resources starting October 1, marking its second round of price increases since May.

Under the new pricing plan, the price of H100 will rise from $3.85 per GPU hour to $4.50, an increase of about 17%; H200 will rise 20% from $4.50 to $5.40; B200 will rise nearly 19% from $7.15 to $8.50; and B300 will rise about 21% from $7.85 per GPU hour to $9.50. 

The changes also extend to CPU-only compute. AMD EPYC Genoa CPU rates will rise 25% to $0.015 per vCPU-hour from $0.012, while Genoa memory will increase about 41% to $0.0045 per GiB-hour from $0.0032. 

The ultimate impact on customers' bills will therefore depend on their configurations and usage.

results.title: Nebius Is Raising On-Demand GPU Prices | The New Money
highlights:
The demand for GPU access is continuing to surge. Which is exactly why Nebius is raising their prices again. What’s happening: 

- Nebius (NASDAQ: NBIS) has publicly stated they are raising on-demand rental prices for Nvidia (NASDAQ: NVDA) GPUs by roughly 17-21% 

Why it matters: 

- This is the second time this year that Nebius has increased the pricing of on-demand GPU capacity 

- Pricing of Nvidia H100s will move up to $4.50 USD per hour, Nvidia H200s will increase to $5.40 USD per hour and Nvidia B200s will go to $8.50 USD per hour 
- Nebius will also increase pricing for Nvidia B300s to $9.50 USD per hour, which represents roughly a 56% jump from where pricing was being offered under six months ago 
- Nebius has been landing a flurry of new major deals lately, including striking a new partnership with Palantir (NASDAQ:PLTR) and a $1B USD deal with artificial intelligence startup Reflection AI

results.title: Nebius to increase prices for Nvidia GPU resources from October By Investing.com
highlights:
Investing.com -- Nebius will raise prices for its on-demand GPU services starting Oct. 1, the company said in an emailed statement, according to Bloomberg News. 

The price increases will apply to Nvidia H100, H200, B200 and B300 GPU resources, according to the statement. The company will also raise rates for certain CPU and memory resources.

The new pricing structure takes effect at the beginning of next month.

Nebius just hiked on-demand GPU rates ~17–21% from Oct 1. H100 goes to $4.50/hr, H200 to $5.40, B200 to $8.50, B300 to $9.50. Second raise since May. B300 is up ~56% from pre-May levels. That is not a price war. That is a sold-out market.

What it actually says: AI compute is still scarce. Customers will pay more to stay on the GPU. Nebius Q2 AI-cloud revenue jumped 514% with visibility past 24 months. CoreWeave already lifted list prices ~25% in July. Peers moved with the news because the sector is pricing power, not discounting.

For neo-clouds like E2E Networks, this is constructive, not threatening.

E2E still lists H100 around ₹256/hr and B200 around ₹664/hr — cheaper than Nebius’s new on-demand book, billed in INR, sitting inside India. As US/EU list prices climb, that gap becomes a sales tool for Indian enterprises, startups, and sovereign workloads that already need data residency. E2E has scaled to ~5,100 GPUs, put a B200 cluster live, and locked a ~₹1,000 Cr Blackwell deal through 2029. Q1 FY27 revenue was up 334% YoY with EBITDA margins near 75%. That is what happens when utilization is high and contracts get longer.

The takeaway is simple. Global neo-clouds raising rates validates the whole category. Regional players with local demand, cheaper headline hours, and multi-year bookings can hold price, mix toward reserved capacity, and keep the operating leverage. The risk is not “AWS will crush them on price.” The risk is CapEx for the next wave of GPUs getting more expensive while they add capacity. Demand is not the debate anymore. Execution and contract quality are.

highlights:
- Nebius Group (NasdaqGS:NBIS) has raised prices for its Nvidia GPU and AMD CPU cloud services in response to strong AI demand. 
- The company cites surging enterprise interest in large-scale AI training and inference workloads as a key driver of the new pricing. 
- Higher rates apply to both Nvidia GPU instances and AMD CPU based compute bundles across Nebius Group's AI focused cloud offerings. 
- The decision to lift Nvidia GPU and AMD CPU cloud pricing reshapes Nebius Group's AI compute economics and client cost base. We have also flagged 4 warning signs (2 major) for Nebius Group.

...

### Why is Nebius Group lifting Nvidia GPU and AMD CPU prices now? 

The move reflects strong AI workloads filling Nebius Group infrastructure and tight supply of high end chips like Nvidia H100 and B300. Higher pricing on GPUs and AMD EPYC Genoa CPUs helps the business align customer bills with the cost of scarce compute capacity and large data center buildouts.
